run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Within the authorized window the hotel-reservation application shows one concrete failure episode at its 09:00 startup and no ongoing fault afterwards. The `user` container panicked while initializing its MongoDB session (`no reachable servers`), exited with code 2 and restarted once; during that gap the frontend returned HTTP 500 on `HTTP POST /user` and `HTTP POST /reservation` because its `/user.User/CheckUser` client span errored. The wrk2 load generator recorded exactly those 2 non-2xx responses in its 09:00:34-09:01:04 round and none afterwards. After `user` registered in Consul at 09:00:37 the whole application is healthy in every signal I checked: all eight service probes return 1, all 19 deployments have 1 ready replica, p95 span latencies are 0.95-4.55 ms (search 2.40 ms), no span exceeds 1000 ms, and the only remaining error-tagged span series are the 4 startup error spans. I also tested the two fault-injection artefacts present in the namespace (`failure-admin-geo`, `failure-admin-rate` scripts mounted into mongodb-geo/mongodb-rate that revoke the admin readWrite role): no authorization failure appears in the MongoDB logs, `rate_requests_rejected_total`/`rate_requests_expired_total`/`search_rate_failures_total`/`search_rate_timeouts_total` are 0, and geo/rate/search show no error spans, so an active privilege-revocation fault is not supported. Two things stay open: the wrk2 client reports ~188-196 socket timeouts per 30 s round in every round with no server-side error or slow span behind them (no baseline, cause unverified), and a blackbox probe of `http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?...` returns probe_success 0 / status code 0 while the cluster holds no Ingress object at all. Data density is very low (pods created 09:00:19-09:00:29; Prometheus span metrics begin ~09:01:30), so no trend or pre-incident baseline can be claimed.

The wrk2 load generator (pod wrk2-job-qjdjf, app=wrk2-job, target http://10.96.240.127:5000) reported for its 09:00:34-09:01:04 round: 2971 requests in 30.04s, "Non-2xx or 3xx responses: 2" and "Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 196"; later rounds logged timeouts 191 (09:01:35) and 188 (09:02:06) with no Non-2xx line.

In the 09:01:36-09:02:06 wrk2 round the recorded latency distribution was mean 3.174 ms, 50% 3.15 ms, 99% 6.61 ms, max 11.008 ms (all sampled values <= 11.12 ms), i.e. the timed-out requests are not reflected as slow responses.

At 2026-11-24T09:02:14Z no hotel-reservation span of any operation exceeded 1000 ms (bucket le="+Inf" minus le="1000" equals 0 for every span_name) and per-service p95 durations were frontend 4.55 ms, geo 0.95 ms, profile 0.96 ms, rate 0.99 ms, recommendation 0.95 ms, reservation 0.95 ms, search 2.40 ms, user 0.95 ms.

A complete sampled GET /hotels trace at 09:02:13Z returns HTTP 200: frontend "HTTP GET /hotels" (5.3 ms) -> frontend client /search.Search/Nearby (3.3 ms) -> search server /search.Search/Nearby (2.8 ms) -> search client /geo.Geo/Nearby (0.6 ms) and /rate.Rate/GetRates (2.1 ms), plus frontend -> /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability and /profile.Profile/GetProfiles; no span carries an error tag.

Direct blackbox probes report probe_success = 1 for frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, search and user services, while the ingress probe "http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095" (job blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation) has probe_success = 0 and probe_http_status_code = 0 with probe_duration_seconds 0.0032.
At query time the cluster returned zero Ingress objects, and the pod list contains no ingress-nginx controller pod.

Rate-service limiter metrics at 09:02:14Z: rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_queue_capacity=256, rate_in_flight=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_requests_received_total=2916 = rate_requests_completed_total=2916, rate_requests_rejected_total=0, rate_requests_expired_total=0; search_requests_total=2435 with search_rate_attempts_total=2435, search_rate_successes_total=2435, search_rate_failures_total=0, search_rate_timeouts_total=0.

Two ConfigMaps exist in hotel-reservation: failure-admin-geo (remove-admin-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh, remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh) and failure-admin-rate (same scripts for rate-db); the revoke scripts call db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'geo-db'|'rate-db'}]) and the remove scripts call db.dropUser('admin'). The mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate deployments mount them at /scripts (configMap failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate), and the rate deployment runs with RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256.

mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate logged only successful authentications for principals admin and root (SCRAM-SHA-1/SCRAM-SHA-256) with no authorization/denied entries in the window, e.g. "Authentication succeeded" for admin from 10.244.7.198 (geo) and from 10.244.7.229 (rate).

All 19 deployments in hotel-reservation had 1 ready/available replica at query time; the only container with kube_pod_container_status_ready = 0 was container "archiver" of audit-log-archiver-29925181-rf55f, whose state is terminated/Completed with exitCode 0 while its fluent-bit-sidecar keeps running, and its logs report "archiver: upload complete ... record=audit-archive-ready". The only pending pod alert is KubePodNotReady for that archiver pod.
No hotel-reservation pod shows CPU throttling above 0.0036 of CFS periods (top value mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-x4zmr 0.0035; all application pods 0) over the 5-minute window ending 09:02:14Z.

The observed impact (2 frontend HTTP 500s at 09:00:34-09:00:36Z) is explained by a startup ordering race: the user container began at ~09:00:22Z while pod mongodb-user-969c6c449-xkbw8 started at 09:00:29Z; the user service does not retry its MongoDB session, so its single dial to mongodb-user:27017 returned "no reachable servers", panicked and restarted, leaving /user.User/CheckUser unavailable until it re-registered at 09:00:37Z.

The ~188-196 wrk2 socket timeouts per 30 s round (about 6.5% of ~2950 requests) are not accompanied by any server-side error span, non-2xx response, or span above 1000 ms in the sampled 09:00:30-09:02:14Z telemetry; they may be a client-side artifact of the load generator's connection/timeout configuration rather than an application symptom, but no baseline or accepted-connection metric was available to decide.

An active privilege-revocation fault from failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate (admin readWrite revoked on geo-db or rate-db) is rejected as the cause of this incident: MongoDB logs show successful admin authentications and no authorization failures, geo/rate/search have no ERROR spans, per-service p95 stays at 0.95-2.40 ms, and rate/search own metrics report 0 rejected, 0 expired, 0 failures and 0 timeouts; no evidence shows either script was executed.

Against a general application outage after the restart: all eight service blackbox probes return 1, all 19 hotel-reservation deployments have 1 ready replica, and the only ERROR-tagged span series in the whole window are the 4 startup spans, while a sampled GET /hotels trace at 09:02:13Z completes with HTTP 200 in 5.3 ms through search, geo, rate, reservation and profile.

Give the user service a bounded retry/backoff around its MongoDB session initialization (or gate its start on mongodb-user readiness with an init container) so a concurrently starting database cannot turn into a panic and a restart, which is the mechanism that produced the two frontend 500s.

To settle the wrk2 timeout question, compare the load generator's timeout setting and its connection-reuse behaviour against a frontend-side accepted-connection/handler-entry metric (net/http or ingress level), and re-run wrk2 against the frontend Service IP with a single-connection and a keep-alive-disabled variant.

gaps: No telemetry exists before the application's 09:00:19-09:00:29 creation: pod logs start at 09:00:20, Jaeger span metrics only begin around 09:01:30 and the sampled traces start at 09:00:34. A pre-incident baseline for latency, error rate and the wrk2 timeout count is therefore missing and no latency trend is claimed.

It is unknown whether the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts were ever executed before or during the window: the cluster has no change history (change_history not integrated), MongoDB is not queryable through the available tools, and executing the scripts would leave no trace in the logs I could read, so the effect of the revoke/drop-admin operations could not be verified.

The wrk2 socket timeouts (~188-196 per 30 s round) cannot be attributed: no accepted-connection, handler-entry or in-flight request metric for the frontend was found in the available metric list, and no span exceeded 1000 ms, so whether the timeouts are a load-generator artifact or dropped connections remains unknown.

The blackbox ingress probe for /api/hotels returns probe_success 0 and probe_http_status_code 0 while the cluster holds no Ingress object and no ingress-nginx controller pod; without history I cannot tell whether this probe was ever served, so I treat its relationship to the hotel-reservation application as unverified.

Pod and object state was read at query time (09:02-09:06), after the incident window closed at 09:02:14, so it cannot prove what the cluster looked like earlier; events cover only their own timestamps inside the window.

The exact endpoint(s) and timeout value used by the wrk2 load generator could not be read because pod wrk2-job-qjdjf and its Job had already been deleted by the time of the query; only its Loki log lines remain.
next_steps: Add a bounded retry or readiness gate for the user service's MongoDB session (see recommendation) and re-run the startup to confirm no panic/restart.

Compare wrk2's timeout setting and connection reuse against a frontend-side accepted-connection metric, or rerun wrk2 against the frontend Service IP with single-connection and no-keep-alive variants, to classify the ~6.5% client timeouts.

Verify out-of-band whether the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate scripts were executed during this run (change/audit history is not integrated here) and, if so, whether the admin user's readWrite role on geo-db/rate-db was restored.

Clarify the intent of the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe: no Ingress object or ingress-nginx controller exists, so that probe target either needs to be created or removed to stop producing a permanent probe_success=0.
Have a human confirm whether the audit-log-archiver KubePodNotReady alert is expected, since the archiver container completes by design and only its sidecar stays running.

The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"
